clue.text: With American backing point skyward and take the air

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the abbreviation for American is turned round

parts.note: a spire is a church's pointed tower aimed at the sky

explanation.surface: A Yank turns, points upward, and steps out for a breath of fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns US into SU before SPIRE is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspire is a literary verb for breathing, drawing in the air.

clue.text: Fur-seal-the main breed

definitions.meaning: a seal valued for its fur
the main is the sea, so this is a kind of animal bred in the sea

explanation.definitionFit: The name is given to the northern fur seal, and taken literally it is a bear of the ocean.

clue.text: Clean though rough growth

explanation.definitionFit: To scour hard is to clean, and scrubland is covered with low bushy vegetation.

clue.text: Here in France the queen would appear less warm

parts.note: ici is the French word for here
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: A French monarch would seem cooler on arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: Something colder is less warm.

clue.text: A viewer's proper place?

parts.note: a viewer read as an eye, and its proper place is the socket or opening it fits

explanation.surface: Where does a television watcher belong?
explanation.definitionFit: An eye socket is the hollow that houses the organ of sight.

clue.text: In here a person may find agricultural workers

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Somebody might come across farm hands in this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals that the letters run across 'here a person'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reapers cut the harvest, so they are farm labourers.

clue.text: Withdraw from touching disquisition

parts.note: re means touching on or concerning
a tract is a treatise or disquisition

explanation.surface: Someone pulls out of an emotional lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to take back or pull in.

clue.text: A macho high-flier-enemy of Israelites

parts.note: macho means manly, male
a kite flies high in the sky

explanation.surface: A tough flyer opposes the tribes of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amalekites were a Biblical people at war with the Israelites.

clue.text: The attempt to get around Eve failed

indicators.note: failed suggests things fell apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An effort to outwit Eve did not succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an earnest try.

clue.text: Forecasters holding races for dogs

indicators.note: holding means one piece wraps round another

parts.note: seers foretell the future
TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Weather forecasters hold dog races.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle races; 'holding' puts it inside SEERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Setters are gundog breeds, such as the Irish and English.

clue.text: Quickest to read, it's being re-written

indicators.note: something being re-written has its letters set down again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that this is the fastest thing to read once rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being re-written' rearranges the letters of TO READ and ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means nimble and deft, so the most adroit is the quickest and handiest.

clue.text: A firm check by all accounts

definitions.text: A firm check by all accounts

parts.words: A firm check by all accounts
parts.note: a company's examination of its books, and 'by all accounts' is a pun since every account is gone through

explanation.surface: Everyone says it is a solid inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: An official inspection of a company's financial records is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: Half of them stop-go stop

indicators.note: Half of takes just the first two of the four letters in them

parts.note: a bar is a barrier that stops passage
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traffic phrase about stop-go driving, with half of them stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' them gives EM; the clue's last 'stop' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, an order halting trade.

clue.text: Made to declare date of birth, as usual

parts.note: to aver is to declare firmly
your date of birth fixes your age

explanation.surface: A clerk makes someone state their birthday, routine paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made to' only links; the date of birth is a loose pointer to how old someone is.
explanation.definitionFit: What is average is ordinary, what normally happens.

clue.text: Call to mind soldiers prayer

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is the regular crossword shorthand for soldiers
a collect is a short prayer in church liturgy

explanation.surface: Troops are reminded of a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: A collect (stress on the first syllable) is a short set prayer of the Anglican church.
explanation.definitionFit: To recollect is to remember, bringing something back to memory.

clue.text: Meeting about heading in the right direction

parts.note: C, from circa, abbreviates about
on course means going the right way

explanation.surface: A gathering discusses getting things on track.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a coming together of people, a gathering.

clue.text: It's the Left one blamed for cut

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
to rate someone is to scold or blame them

explanation.surface: The Left gets the blame for budget cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's the' only links; 'rate' in the old sense of telling off.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerated means torn or slashed, wounded.

clue.text: Figures one pores over

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
to con is to study closely

explanation.surface: Somebody studies statistics carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Icons are images or symbolic figures, such as religious portraits.

clue.text: Pick-me-up for heavyweight in charge

parts.note: a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: A boxing champion takes a restorative drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a medicine or drink that restores energy.

clue.text: Those taking a little rest sat sprawling

indicators.note: sprawling suggests limbs flung about, so the letters spread into a new order

explanation.surface: People who lounged in a heap took a short rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasters sample food or drink in small amounts.

clue.text: The sedum soon crept all over the place

indicators.note: letters scattered all over the place are jumbled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A gardener's plant spread quickly across the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges SOON CREPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonecrop is a common name for the sedum, a succulent rock plant.

clue.text: A cleaner, small, very small, and quietly hesitant

parts.note: wee is Scottish for tiny
P, piano, means quietly in music
er is a hesitant noise

explanation.surface: A tiny, timid cleaner speaks softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeper cleans floors or chimneys by brushing.

clue.text: Advanced after none turned up worth much

indicators.note: after places the piece for advanced at the end

parts.note: O, zero, means none

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the word up is read backwards

parts.note: lent means advanced as a loan

explanation.surface: Money was loaned once nothing showed up of any value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses UP to PU; 'after' sets LENT behind O PU.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means wealthy, rich in money.

clue.text: Page on an area of Spain that's ideal

parts.note: Aragon is a region of north-eastern Spain

explanation.surface: A page about a Spanish region that is perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'that's' only link; 'ideal' is a noun here, a perfect model.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a model of perfection, an ideal example.

clue.text: Gush about the top man's cat

indicators.note: about here means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a surge is a sudden gush
CO, the commanding officer, is the man at the top of a unit

explanation.surface: The boss's pet cat gushes about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip, not a pet; 'about' puts CO inside SURGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip used for flogging is called a cat (cat-o'-nine-tails), and a lash is a flogging instrument.

clue.text: Questionable nuclear explosion

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters apart so they land in new places

explanation.surface: A dubious atomic blast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open to question is doubtful, not plain.

clue.text: Petition causing many to talk wildly

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral 100, stands for many
to rave is to talk wildly

explanation.surface: A plea that sets a crowd ranting.
explanation.definitionFit: To crave is to beg or plead, as a petitioner does.

clue.text: Choice not all feel it easy to make

indicators.note: not all means only some letters of the run following are used

explanation.surface: Not everyone finds it simple to make a decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all' signals letters within 'feel it easy'; 'Choice' is an adjective, the best.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the choicest, the pick of the group.

clue.text: Some regrettably flighty creature

indicators.note: Some means only part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A few silly animals are behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals letters inside 'regrettably'; 'flighty' means able to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: This heron is a bird, a creature that takes flight.

clue.text: Setting up new paper round

indicators.note: new tells us the word paper is made afresh in another order

parts.note: a ring is a round shape

explanation.surface: A newsagent organises a fresh delivery route.
explanation.definitionFit: Preparing something is getting it ready, arranging it beforehand.

clue.text: A poet's no penny-pincher!

definitions.meaning: Stephen ... was an English twentieth-century poet
someone who lavishes money rather than hoarding it

explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Spender was a noted English poet, and a big spender is the opposite of a miser.

clue.text: Article written on control inside

parts.note: the is the definite article
a rein is a means of control

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is written about restraint within.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein means in that place, within it.
